title: SIEM connector playbook — Splunk / Datadog / Sentinel
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures the requirements, expected audit schema mappings, and connector specs for SIEM exports from Redwood Inference. Focus: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs API, and Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics HTTP Data Collector). Goal: enable customers and internal ops to onboard secure, monitored, and auditable log exports that satisfy enterprise compliance and evidence automation needs.

Audience:
- Security & compliance engineers (internal or customer)
- Platform / SRE teams doing connector maintenance
- Solutions engineering / sales when scoping customer requirements

Doc status and usage notes:
- This is an operational playbook and intentionally pragmatic: examples, curl snippets, field maps, tactical retries and rate-limit guidance.
- Changes to audit schema (redwood audit v2) must update the mapping table below and trigger PR to rw-infra. See linked artifacts.

High-level requirements (customer perspective):
1) Secure transport: TLS 1.2+ mandatory, mutual TLS where customer requests private deployment, HMAC/Token auth otherwise.
2) Integrity & tamper detection: all exported batches should include sequence_id + signature header (HMAC-SHA256) for high-risk customers.
3) RBAC considerations: the connector should only expose 'read-only' audit/export credentials. Use RBAC v2 groups: siem-exporter role (minimal privileges).
4) Retention & sampling: customers can request full retention or sampled export. Default: export all AUTH, CONFIG_CHANGE, ACCESS events; sample INFO/DEBUG at 1%.
5) Evidence automation: exported payloads must contain evidence_id which maps to internal evidence store for automated attachments during audits.
6) Throughput & rate-limit expectations: default hosted export connection supports bursts up to 2000 events/minute; higher needs negotiated dedicated capacity.

Export payload & canonical fields:
(We rely on a canonical SIEM schema to make mapping predictable; everything below is strings/flat fields.)
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC (e.g., 2026-02-14T18:23:44Z)
- event_id: UUID v4
- sequence_id: incremental per-tenant export batch id
- tenant_id: customer org id (GUID)
- service: which Redwood service produced event (e.g., api, runtime, deployment)
- actor: principal that initiated action (user:email or service:role)
- actor_type: user | service | system
- action: canonical action name (LOGIN, CREATE_KEY, MODEL_DEPLOY, GENERATE_TOKEN, ROLLOUT_START, ROLLOUT_FAIL, INFERENCE_CALL)
- result: success | failure | partial
- resource_type: model | deployment | key | route | project
- resource_id: identifier (short string)
- request_id: internal request trace id (if applicable)
- client_ip: IP address if available
- region: Redwood region code serving the request
- latency_ms: numeric rounded to milliseconds for inference and API calls
- quality_metrics: JSON-stringified map for inference quality (when present) — e.g., "{"perplexity":24.3}" (we recommend pushing this only to Datadog/Sentinel, not Splunk HEC by default due to size)
- evidence_id: internal evidence pointer for compliance workflows
- raw_payload: optional base64 payload for full event (use sparingly)
- tags: comma-separated string of tags

Notes on field sizing and indexing:
- Avoid very large raw_payload fields. If raw artifacts >32KB, store in evidence store and include evidence_id only.
- Mark tenant_id, event_id, timestamp as indexed in the SIEM mapping to enable fast queries.

Splunk HEC connector spec (recommended defaults):
- Endpoint: https://input-prd-redwood.splunkcloud.com:8088/services/collector/event/1.0
- Auth: HEC token in Authorization header: "Splunk <token>". HMAC signature header optional: X-RW-Signature: sha256=<hex>
- Batch format: JSON array of events or newline-delimited JSON (preferNDJSON). Max batch size: 1MB or 5000 events (whichever comes first).
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max 6 retries, 10s initial delay.
- Error handling: on 4xx -> drop (bad event), 429 -> backoff and retry, 5xx -> retry. Log failures to internal monitoring.
- Recommended Splunk index mapping: map timestamp->_time, tenant_id->tenant, event_id->event_id, service->sourcetype (or set sourcetype to rw:audit), resource_type->object_type.
- HEC config notes: set send-mode=JSON, enable ack=1 for high-assurance customers (ack per event) but beware throughput reduction.

Datadog Logs API connector spec (recommended defaults):
- Endpoint: https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input
- Auth: API key as query param ?api_key=<key> or DD-API-KEY header. For higher security, use Datadog API key stored in KMS and rotated.
- Format: Datadog recommends newline delimited JSON, each event with "ddsource": "redwood", "service": "redwood-inference" and attributes under "attributes" map.
- Rate limits: Document default account limits (customer-specific); our hosted export should aggregate and throttle to not exceed. Default safe throughput: 1000 events/min per tenant.
- Retry: 4 retries, linear backoff (5s increments) then escalate to dedicated queue.
- Mappings: timestamp->timestamp, tenant_id->attributes.tenant_id, event_id->attributes.event_id, severity mapped from action/result to DD severity tags.
- Enrichment: send cloud.metadata (region, cluster) as attributes.

Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics HTTP Data Collector) connector spec:
- Endpoint pattern: https://<workspaceId>.ods.opinsights.azure.com/api/logs?api-version=2016-04-01
- Auth: API signature header (Authorization) built as per Microsoft docs (shared key). Support for AAD-based ingestion should be evaluated for private deployments.
- Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 (can accept arrays of records)
- Schema: set "LogType" to RW_Audit and include tenant_id, event_id, action as top-level properties. Ensure record size < 32KB.
- Retry & throttling: Azure will reply 429 when throttled; implement exponential backoff + persistent queue. For high-volume customers, recommend direct Azure Event Hub integration and partner connector.

Authentication and secrets handling:
- All tokens stored in KMS with automatic rotation where supported.
- For hosted connectors, minimal set of scopes/privileges: read:audit_logs and read:service_metadata.
- For private deployments, offer option for customer-managed credentials (customer provides Splunk HEC token or Datadog key). Document mutual TLS configuration steps.

RBAC v2 implications and mapping:
- Create a dedicated role "siem-exporter" in RBAC v2 with a constrained permission set: can_read_audit_logs, can_list_evidence, can_read_tenant_metadata. No ability to create or revoke keys.
- Audit log entries generated by the connector must themselves carry a system_actor value (service:siem-connector) to avoid confusion for downstream investigations.

Evidence automation and attachments:
- Field evidence_id in exported events must be resolvable in the Evidence Store API: GET /evidence/{evidence_id} returns signed URL & metadata.
- If the event references large artifacts, include evidence_url (short-lived signed URL) and evidence_hash (sha256).
- Automation workflow: SIEM alert references evidence_id -> Auto-attach evidence to case in ticketing tool (Jira/ServiceNow) via webhook.

Onboarding checklist for a new customer SIEM export (playbook steps):
1) Collect destination details and auth method (Splunk HEC token / Datadog key / Sentinel workspace+key).
2) Confirm TLS and optional mTLS requirements.
3) Agree on event scope (full vs sampled), retention expectations, and rate limits.
4) Generate exporter credentials in RBAC v2 and add to KMS vault; provide the customer with instructions if customer-managed.
5) Create initial field mapping and test index/LogType configuration on customer side.
6) Run staged validation with 1000 events, verify ingestion, timestamps, timezone alignment, and dedup keys.
7) Enable ack mode for Splunk if requested; run throughput test.
8) Document SLA and escalation path for missed exports.

Validation and QA tests (automation-friendly):
- Test 1: Schema validation suite — send malformed payloads and verify 4xx/400 handling.
- Test 2: Signature verification — verify HMAC fails when signature mismatch.
- Test 3: Backpressure simulation — simulate 429 from SIEM and assert exponential backoff and queueing.
- Test 4: Retention evidence lookup — for a sample evidence_id, call Evidence Store API and confirm artifact integrity.

Monitoring and observability for the connector:
- Expose metrics via Prometheus/Grafana (for hosted infra): export_success_count, export_failure_count, last_export_timestamp, queue_depth, avg_latency_ms, backoff_retries_total.
- Send connector health events to internal audit stream with actor=service:siem-connector and action=EXPORT_HEALTHCHECK.
- Create out-of-band alerting when failure rate >1% for 5m or queue_depth > threshold.

Troubleshooting common failure modes:
- 401/403: check token rotation and RBAC role permissions; verify token present in KMS and not expired.
- 429: downsample events or request higher capacity; implement per-tenant throttling.
- 413 / 413 Request Entity Too Large: split batches smaller and enforce 32KB per record / 1MB per batch.
- Signature mismatches: confirm time skew, ensure canonical string used for HMAC.

Privacy & PII handling:
- PII-level fields should be redacted unless customer explicitly requests raw payloads. Use evidence_id pattern to link to encrypted evidence store for full artifacts.
- Default export mask: redact user.email for normal exports; allow opt-in for full detail for enterprise customers with DPA.

Versioning and change management:
- Connector spec versioning: major.minor (e.g., 1.0). Incompatible changes to canonical fields require 90-day notice to customers.
- Keep changelog in Confluence and tag releases in GitHub infra repo.

Appendix: example payloads
- Example NDJSON event for Splunk: {"timestamp":"2026-02-14T18:23:44Z","event_id":"0f8fad5b-d9cb-469f-a165-70867728950e","tenant_id":"org_1234","service":"api","actor":"user:alice@example.com","action":"MODEL_DEPLOY","result":"success","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"m-rtx-042","evidence_id":"ev-9876"}

- Example Datadog envelope snippet: {"ddsource":"redwood", "service":"redwood-inference", "attributes": {"tenant_id":"org_1234", "event_id":"0f8fad..."}, "message": "MODEL_DEPLOY success", "timestamp": 1707956624 }

Open questions & TODOs (for security and s2s teams):
- Decide default sampling policy for DEBUG-level events (proposal: 0.5% global). (Owner: Rajan)
- Add AAD-based ingestion path for Sentinel private deploys. (Owner: Wei)
- Finalize HMAC header format and add to API reference. (Owner: Elena)
